column3: Directly specifies entry into an intensely hot fire, grounding the warned outcome.
Adds the summons to protective caution that frames a warning's intended response.
Contrast route marks the punitive-fire boundary without supplying positive route support.
Makes warning an explicit, active commission.
Names denial as the immediate contrary disposition within the focus passage.
Adds a precedent of denial followed by the tested reality of warning and punishment.
Parallels a named, blazing fire and adds its sustained, fueled character.
Immediately restricts who encounters the fire announced in 92:14.
Adds the image of a deliberately fueled fire, though the basic fire outcome is established earlier.
Supplies the latent-to-kindled movement of fire, secondary to the warning scene.
States that the impending outcome cannot be repelled.
Shows fire as an inescapable hostile dispatch, not a neutral substance.
Links wrongful acts to being brought into fire after all help fails.
Immediately supplies the protected counterparty to the fire of 92:14.
Adds enclosure and confinement to the announced fire.
Connects transgression and injustice to being made to enter fire.
Contributes the light-manifestation pole that supports the passage's warning contrast.
Fire as created substance does not materially clarify the warning or its outcome.
Adds rejection of accumulated warnings, but repeats an already established pattern.
Depicts compelled movement into the fire, sharpening its unavoidable consequence.
Reiterates intensely hot fire without adding much beyond earlier direct parallels.
Reaffirms the bounded role of the messenger as a warner.
Names affirmation of the good as the positive disposition in the immediate passage.
Shows fulfilled punishment retrospectively validating prior warning.
Establishes the repeated sending of warners among a people.
Contributes the darkness pole in the passage's surrounding contrast.
Connects the present warning to earlier warners and their precedents.
Defines the messenger's role as clear warning, with little further specificity.
Presents a beneficial, guiding use of fire; it is only a distant contrast to 92:14.
Adds illuminating written evidence, secondary to the fire warning itself.
Shows warning becoming an announced catastrophic consequence after turning away.
Sets the divergent striving that the focus passage's outcomes subsequently divide.
Explicitly joins conveyed messages, disobedience, and enduring hellfire.
Shows warning activating fear and caution, but repeats the response theme.
Begins the immediate positive path contrasted with the fire-bound path.
Only loosely relates fire to denial of meaningful creation.
Adds human kindling of fire, a secondary aspect of its active character.
Makes wrongdoing an inward fire already being consumed, then an ensuing blaze.
Contrast route supplies a boundary image of being dragged into fire.
Directly announces being made to enter Saqar.
Adds the failure of wealth at the point of downfall in the immediate sequence.
Frames fire as a danger requiring prior self-protection, directly serving the warning function.
Adds the kindling of hellfire, but is otherwise a repeated fire image.
States guidance as the divine counterpart to the passage's warning.
Contrast route confirms fire as punitive recompense, without positive route support.
Asks what caused entry into Saqar, opening the causal side of the warning.
Places warning beside testimony and good news, with limited new detail.
Concerns objections to a messenger rather than the warned fire.
Affirms the certainty of punishment, reinforcing the warning's seriousness.
Clarifies the immediate passage's purified giving as non-reciprocal.
The designation as fire-companions adds little beyond prior consequence cards.
Beneficial fire and guidance form only a remote contrast to 92:14.
Identifies the protected person's purifying giving immediately before the final reward.
Repeats the retrospective warning-and-punishment pattern already supplied.
Repeats the beneficial-fire scene with no closer link to the focus.
Presents fire as an actual ordeal that exposes and tests, not merely an announced threat.
Adds a shared, enduring fire outcome to a destructive relation.
Connects crossing divinely set limits with enduring, humiliating fire.
Completes the immediate motive of the protected giver in the focus passage.
Adds fire prepared and fueled by people and stones, though the central outcome is redundant.
Adds recurring bodily experience of punishment within the fire.
The paired creation motif is surrounding structure, not a close clarification of 92:14.
Contrast route establishes the limit of rescue from fire.
Explains that warning can fail through the recipient's closed response.
Makes fire's scorching exposure concrete through its effect on faces.
Shows warning voiced in protective concern before a great-day punishment.
Provides a light-lost contrast that modestly supports the warning's visibility dimension.
Names the denier who turns away as the immediate referent of 92:15.
Addresses the fire previously denied, directly joining denial, warning, and encounter.
Adds an enclosing fire and an inhospitable relief, intensifying the announced consequence.
Records surprise at a warner but adds little to warning's function or outcome.
Contrasts fire-companions with the successful garden-companions.
Uses fire as a technical instrument, without bearing on the warning or punitive fire.
Adds insight and reminder as antecedents to responsive warning.
Directly depicts a kindled divine fire reaching inward, though it repeats the core outcome.
Restates the clear-warner role without further connection.
Adds the bodily atmosphere of those in fire, secondary to the core warning.
Makes warning a mercy given where prior warning had not arrived.
The record of spending and vows has no specific route to the warning fire.
Connects diversion from the path and temporary enjoyment to return to fire.
Links brief enjoyment and fire only generally, with no distinctive clarification.
Explicitly joins reminder, warning, protective caution, and mercy.
States hell as a terrible settled destination after the earlier path diversion.
Contrast route marks persistent excess as belonging with fire.
War-fire imagery is not the punitive fire or warning process of 92:14.
Clarifies that warning can be plain while the timing of the outcome remains withheld.
The fire-companion formula repeats a general outcome without new insight.
A vow scene has no material connection to the focus.
Shows an ignored warning becoming known through an experienced destructive sign.
Shows one revealed message functioning as warning for some and reminder for believers.
Turns a familiar life-giving form into the bad outcome of those warned.
Locates the warning commission in the messenger's heart, a secondary role detail.
Defines a clear warner's role as faithful public transmission of received revelation.
Reinforces that an unreceptive disposition can render warning and non-warning alike.
Fire destroying a garden is only a remote illustrative use.
Places warners within a larger guidance and adjudication pattern, but is less specific.
Adds the permanence of not leaving fire after regretful separation.
Pairs good news and warning as complementary guidance functions.
Family maintenance instructions do not clarify 92:14.
Fire as a basis for arrogant comparison does not clarify the warning or its consequence.
Completes the immediate positive path by promising facilitation toward ease.
Introduces the immediate contrary path of withholding and self-sufficiency.
Completes that contrary path with facilitation toward hardship before the fire warning.
States the encompassing divine claim that frames the warning's authority.
Supplies the final satisfaction promised to the protected giver, completing the passage's contrast.
Names the blazing fire with the same distinctive l-z-y root as 92:14.
Adds fire's stripping, consuming force to the shared blazing-fire image.
Directly identifies the one who turned away as summoned by that fire.
Connects gathering and hoarding to the same fire, closely matching 92:11's failed wealth.
Frames reminder as purposeful admonition before the divided responses.
Identifies reverent fear as the receptive response to admonition.
Names the wretched person's avoidance of the reminder, directly paralleling 92:15.
States that this wretched person enters the greatest fire.
Adds the fire's condition of neither dying nor living.
Intensifies the already linked Saqar announcement through an interrogative disclosure.
Describes Saqar as leaving nothing and sparing nothing.
Adds Saqar's visible scorching of human beings.
Makes the fire's guardians and number a trial, joining warning to response and disbelief.
Begins the answer explaining what led people into Saqar.
Names neglect of prayer among the causes of entry into Saqar.
Adds immersion with the false or futile as another cause.
Names denial of the Day of Recompense among those causes.
Shows that intercession does not benefit those who rejected the warning.
Introduces transgression as the condition contrasted with the reverent path.
Adds preferring the worldly life as the transgressor's disposition.
Identifies hellfire as that disposition's abode.
Introduces fear of standing before the Lord as the counter-disposition.
Completes that counter-disposition with restraint from desire and the garden outcome.
Announces certain sight of the blaze, making the warned reality manifest.
Intensifies that encounter into sight with certainty.
States hellfire as the destination of those who disbelieve.
Adds the fire's audible raging and boiling reception.
Depicts it as nearly bursting with rage, intensifying the warning scene.
Directly asks whether a warner came before entry into the blaze.
Links refusal to hear or reason with becoming companions of the blaze.
Adds acknowledgement of sin after the warning has been rejected.
Explicitly connects denial of the fire to repeated return into it and tasting its punishment.
Defines warning as being given through revelation and notes the deaf recipient's non-response.
Calls the rejecters and what they worship fuel for hell.
Adds the enduring cry and lack of hearing within the fire.
Commands warning of the Day of Regret while people remain heedless.
Places every person in relation to passing by the hellfire, heightening the warning's scope.
Directly contrasts rescue of the reverent with abandonment of wrongdoers in it.
Combines arrival at hell with the question of whether warners brought the signs.
Directly commands protective caution against the fire prepared for disbelievers.
Presents seeking protection from the punishment of fire as a central supplication.
Presents seeking protection from the fire's punishment as the believers' plea.
Establishes that denial and disbelief meet the fire without excuse on that day.
Adds chains, restraints, and a blazing fire as the prepared punishment for deniers.
Adds a prepared fire alongside bonds and choking food in an eschatological warning.
Depicts hell as lying in wait for transgressors.
Directly commands that the condemned person be made to burn in hellfire.
States entry into a blaze as the consequence of receiving the record behind one's back.
Establishes the principle that punishment follows the sending of a messenger.
Links warning by revelation with protective fear before gathering to the Lord.
Defines the Quranic warning as directed to a contentious people while bringing good news to the reverent.
States that revealed warning may awaken protective fear or remembrance.
Shows that a prior messenger removes the claim that punishment came without warning.
Describes warning reaching a people whose forebears had not been warned.
Identifies the one who follows the reminder and fears the Merciful unseen as responsive to warning.
Pairs good news and warning in the revealed Arabic message.
Connects revealed warning with the Day of Gathering and divided outcomes.
Directs warning by the Quran toward whoever fears the divine threat.
Presents the messenger as a clear warner while calling people to flee toward God.
States Noah's commission as a clear warner to his people.
Connects worship, protective caution, and obedience to Noah's warning.
Calls the revelation a warning for humankind, providing the wider frame for 74:2.
